title: slice-aggregate-cost-latency-ux-hypotheses
content:
Summary:
This note captures a different approach to token-level cost and latency visibility: instead of a single per-invocation inspector, present a slice-and-aggregate UX that lets engineers define arbitrary "slices" of traffic (by route, prompt template, user cohort, model variant, streaming vs non-streaming, etc.), see token-level decomposition within that slice, and then flip to an aggregated rollup that highlights outlier contributions to cost and tail latency.

Why new?
- Current wires focus on per-invocation drilldown (useful for debugging a specific request).
- We need a workflow for product teams who want to:
  1) identify which prompt templates drive the most cost across a fleet,
  2) quantify latency hot spots attributable to model KV cache misses vs batching inefficiencies,
  3) prioritize optimizations (caching, prefixed prompts, quantized model variants) with an expected ROI.
- This doc is a working set of UX hypotheses + simple wire sketches + grooming backlog to validate the slice-first experience.

Users and personas prioritized here:
- Platform engineers (SRE/infra) — want root-cause signals and SLO impact views.
- ML engineers / infra-ops — want model variant comparisons and quantized vs full comparisons.
- Product managers / growth engineers — want to know which flows cost most and where product changes yield savings.

Top-level goals (product outcomes):
- Reduce 95th-token latency SLO violations by 25% for targeted products within 90 days of instrumenting slices.
- Surface top-5 prompt templates by cost per DAU for faster product decisions.
- Provide a stable path from slice discovery -> rollback-enabled optimization (e.g., toggle caching or route to cheaper model) with simulated cost delta.

Key concepts / glossary used in the wire:
- Slice: a query (filter) composed of (route, prompt_template_id, model_family, region, customer_tier, streaming_flag). Multiple slices can overlap.
- Atomic contribution: token-level source attribution (system/prompt/instr vs user prompt vs model completion vs tooling/metadata tokens).
- Aggregate rollup: summary view of a slice showing cost per-invocation, tokens per-phase, median/95/99 latency distribution, and predicted monthly spend.
- Heuristic buckets: common groupings (prompt vs completion, high-prefix vs short-ask, streaming vs batch) used to bootstrap slicer.

Wireframe variants (A/B/C) — text descriptions for quick prototyping:
- Variant A: "Explorer-first"
  - Left rail: slice builder (autocomplete filters + saved slices + quick templates: top-templates, high-95-latency, high-token-count).
  - Main: aggregate card for selected slice (sparkline for cost & 95th latency), below that a stacked bar showing token-phase breakdown over time (system/prompt/completion).
  - Right rail: top contributing invocation examples (sampled), with ability to open per-invocation inspector.
  - Pros: fast discovery, aligns with metrics-first workflows.
  - Cons: can overwhelm non-technical PMs.

- Variant B: "Runbook mode"
  - Top: guided diagnostic flow (Detect -> Inspect -> Simulate -> Act).
  - Detect: auto-suggested slices generated by heuristics (e.g., >X% cost increase MoM or 95th latency spike).
  - Inspect: quick inline micro-profiles for the top 3 invocations in the slice.
  - Simulate: quick toggles to simulate rerouting to cheaper model or enabling prefix cache; shows estimated cost/latency delta.
  - Act: one-click create rollout/canary with pre-filled config and a GitHub PR link.
  - Pros: action-oriented; shorter path from problem to fix.

- Variant C: "Research table"
  - Spreadsheet-style pivot: rows are prompt templates, columns = metrics (mean tokens, median latency, 95th latency, cost per 1k calls).
  - Inline cell expansion shows sampled invocations and a mini-sparkline.
  - Pros: familiar to PMs/data teams; good for prioritization.

Instrumentation and backend notes (feasibility):
- Required event fields: prompt_template_id, model_variant, tokens_by_phase (system/prompt/completion), token_count, per-token-latency-breakdown if feasible, KV-cache-hit-flag, batching-window-ms, request_size_bytes, streaming_flag.
- We can approximate per-token latency by attributing total gen latency across completion tokens, but precise per-token timings require runtime hooks (we have some of these in serving-runtime trace).
- Suggest incremental rollout: begin with aggregated signals using existing logs (token_count, total_gen_latency, model_variant) and add token-phase extraction in next release.
- For simulations (Simulate in Variant B) we'll run a cost-model that applies per-token unit price, model multiplier, and a latency delta heuristic for model-route changes. Maintain conservative bounds so estimations don't promise false savings.

Metrics & KPIs to display by default for any slice:
- Invocation count (period)
- Tokens per invocation (median, p95)
- Cost per invocation (median, p95) and cost per 10k requests
- Latency distribution: median, p95, p99 for full invocation and for 'generation' phase
- % of invocations streaming vs non-streaming
- % of invocations with KV-cache-miss (if available)
- Top prompt templates by contribution to total spend (sorted)
- Estimated monthly spend for slice at current traffic levels

Example grooming backlog (rough priorities):
- P0: implement slice builder UI component + saved slices storage (JIRA-3141).
- P0: backend aggregated slice API (filters -> returns aggregate metrics) using existing logs (JIRA-3142).
- P1: instrument token-phase extraction at serving runtime and pipe into observability stream (JIRA-3180).
- P1: wire Variant B Simulate prototype on frontend (JIRA-3192).
- P2: add one-click rollout template for 'route to cheaper model' with pre-flight safety checks (JIRA-3210).
- P2: export CSV/pivot view (Variant C) and scheduled slice reports to Slack/email (JIRA-3225).

Acceptance criteria (for MVP slice-aggregate view):
- Frontend shows a slice builder + aggregate card.
- Backend returns: invocation count, avg tokens, median & p95 latency, cost estimate for the slice (computed from current pricing model) for a 7d window.
- Users can save a slice and pin it to a dashboard.
- For saved slices, the system auto-detects anomalies (spike detection) and surfaces an in-app alert.

Open questions & decisions to make:
- How many dimensions should the slice builder surface by default? (recommendation: start with route, model_family, prompt_template_id, region, customer_tier).
- Sampling rate for per-invocation examples (we have storage limits). Do we keep a reservoir sampler per slice?
- Simulation accuracy threshold: what delta % do we consider acceptable to show to users?
- Rollout safety: what automatic rollback conditions should be required (error rate bump, latency SLO breach)?

Low-fi ASCII wire (main aggregate card):
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Slice: "signup-flow / model-gptx / prod-us"  [saved]  [run]
| Cost sparkline      | 95th latency sparkline               [Simulate]
|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Invocation count: 12,200   |  tokens / inv (median): 420      |
| cost / inv (median): $0.012 | cost /10k: $120                  |
| stack-bar: [sys: 5%][prompt: 30%][completion: 65%]            |
| Top templates by spend: template#: 43 (32%), 17 (18%), 209 (9%)|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+

Next steps for this doc:
- Quick hallway tests with 4 teams (SRE, infra-ml, growth PM, solutions eng) to validate the three variants. Put a shared Loom + prototype by end of next week.
- Groom JIRA P0s with owners and estimate backend implementation cost.
- Prototype cost-simulation math in a sandbox repo (PR link above).

Notes to reviewers (things I'd like feedback on):
- Is "slice-first" mental model accessible enough for PMs? Or do we need to ship a separate "templates" entrypoint?
- Which slice heuristics would you want auto-suggested? (e.g., >20% of cost in last 7 days, or 95th latency increase >2x)
- Feels like Variant B "Runbook mode" will map best to our canary + rollout plumbing — opinions?

Quick contact list: Priya Rao (product), Dante Alvarez (infra), Maya Thompson (ux), Liam O'Neill (platform-eng).

End of doc.
